name: Kyrgyz-Ata National Park
near: Kalday — a village/gorge at the park entrance, about 2.5 km from the catalog point (OSM); recommended as the entry point and a place to find a local guide (central-asia.guide). The base town is Nookat (bus station, ~25–30 km to the north); the road heads toward Eski-Nookat (Nomad's Land).
elev: About 2000–2400 m in the main (tourist) part (Central Asia Travel; Nomad's Land — 2400 m). The heights of the peaks on the northern slope of the Alay Range within the park boundaries are not confirmed.
short: Kyrgyz-Ata is a nature park (since 1992, 11,172 ha) on the northern slope of the Alay Range in Nookat district: juniper forests, the marble canyons of Karagoy, Kalday and Mazar, mineral springs and petroglyphs.
desc: The Kyrgyz-Ata State Nature Park was established on 18 March 1992 to preserve and restore juniper forests, mountain tulips and saffron; its area is 11,172 ha (Nomad's Land, Central Asia Travel). The park occupies a river basin on the northern slope of the Alay Range (Pamir-Alay) at an elevation of about 2000–2400 m: limestone and marble cliffs with coloured veins, the deep gorges of Karagoy (the most popular), Kalday and Mazar, the mineral springs of Tuya-Muyun and Eski-Nookat, ancient settlements, burial grounds and petroglyphs (too.kg, Central Asia Travel). Dirt roads lead to most of the gorges; there is almost no mobile signal or formal infrastructure, and there are many places to camp (too.kg). In July 2026 an automated checkpoint with cashless payment was installed at the entrance, and from August 2026 a new entrance arch, checkpoint and wastewater treatment facilities are being built (time.kg, economist.kg, Kaktus).
guide: Kyrgyz-Ata is the nearest real mountain forest to Osh: ancient juniper, marble cliffs with coloured veins and clear streams. Start with the Karagoy gorge — it is the most popular, with picnic and camping spots — and then look into Kalday and Mazar. The park is quiet and sparsely visited, the trails are almost unmarked, so a local guide from Kalday will make the walk much easier. There is almost no mobile signal anywhere, except, according to reviews, Beeline — warn your family in advance. The park is also good as an acclimatization stop before the Pamirs: 2000–2400 m is exactly what you need for a first night in the mountains.
see: The gorges of Karagoy (the main walking area), Kalday and Mazar; juniper forests; marble cliffs with coloured veins; the mineral springs of Tuya-Muyun and Eski-Nookat; petroglyphs (rock drawings of animals in the Aravan canyon), ancient settlements and burial grounds; in spring — mountain tulips and saffron (too.kg, Central Asia Travel, dwc.kg).
skip: You expect a developed park with marked trails, cafes and mobile signal — there is almost none of that here. You have no car and no time for a day trip from Osh. You are already heading to Sary-Chelek or Arslanbob and want forests specifically — the infrastructure there is better.
diff: Easy-moderate: day walks and horse rides through the gorges, the trails are unmarked and sometimes confusing (TripAdvisor). The altitude of 2000–2400 m is suitable for acclimatization (dwc.kg, Central Asia Travel).
when: May — September: tulips and saffron bloom in spring, in summer it is cool in the juniper forest at 2000+ m; TripAdvisor reviews — May — August. In winter the dirt roads may be impassable (editorial).
hours: The checkpoint's official opening hours are not published. Since July 2026 an automated checkpoint with cashless payment has operated at the entrance (time.kg, 28.07.2026); since 14.08.2026 a new entrance complex is under construction — check the access route and whether the checkpoint is working before you go (ilovekg).
daytime: Leave Osh in the morning: the drive is ~2 h, a walk through the gorges takes more than 3 hours (TripAdvisor), and towards evening it gets dark quickly in the gorges (editorial).
how: Osh → Nookat (highway west, ~45 km) → south on the road toward Eski-Nookat and Kalday → dirt roads to the Karagoy/Kalday/Mazar gorges. About 2 h by car from Osh (Central Asia Travel). The often-quoted “40 km from Osh” is an understatement: it is ~54 km to the park as the crow flies, and roughly 70–80 km by road (calculation, not confirmed by a navigator). There are few signs to the park (TripAdvisor).
needcar: Yes: there is no public transport all the way to the park; take a marshrutka (minibus)/shared taxi to Nookat, then a taxi to Kalday/the gorges. Your own car or a tour is more convenient.
self: Yes, by your own car or by taxi from Nookat; no border permit needed (the park is not on the border-zone list — tour.too.kg). The trails are unmarked and locals know little about the park — bring an offline map and ask for directions in Kalday (central-asia.guide, TripAdvisor).
roadtype: Paved road Osh — Nookat, then rural roads and “good quality” dirt roads to most of the gorges (too.kg); the condition of the different approaches varies.
traveltime: About 2 h by car from Osh (Central Asia Travel). By public transport — Osh → Nookat + taxi, roughly 2.5–3 h (editorial).
stay: Camping — many spots in the gorges (too.kg); Kyrgyz-Ata Yurt Camp — a yurt camp (TripAdvisor 5/5, 1 review from 2019; prices not published); guesthouses/yurts in the gorges — by arrangement (Central Asia Travel mentions this indirectly). No current 2025–2026 prices found.
net: There is no mobile signal over most of the territory (too.kg); according to reviews, Beeline is the only operator that gets a signal in Kyrgyz-Ata (bestofosh).
entry: An entry fee is charged (Nomad's Land); since July 2026 it is paid through the automated checkpoint by card, QR code or e-wallet (time.kg, 28.07.2026). The tariff amount was not found in open sources for 2024–2026 — check at the checkpoint/with the park administration.
transfer: Not confirmed: prices for a taxi Nookat — Kalday and for CBT tours are not published in the sources found.
bring: Cash and a bank card/QR app to pay the entry fee; food and water (there are few shops near the stops — TripAdvisor); a bag for rubbish (there are no bins on the trails); offline maps; a warm sweater for the evening; tick repellent (editorial).
warn: There are almost no signs or trail markings — it is easy to get lost (TripAdvisor). No mobile signal (except Beeline in places). The entrance is being rebuilt (2026) — the access route may change. The “Kyrgyz-Ata” point in Google Maps leads to the administration office near Nookat, not into the park. Protected area: campfires, cutting juniper and picking plants (tulips, saffron) are restricted by the park regime (editorial, based on protected-area status).
food: Not confirmed: no cafe in the park was found. In Nookat and along the road — southern Kyrgyz cuisine (plov, samsa — editorial, specific places not checked); bring a picnic.
reviews: TripAdvisor “Kyrgyz Ata National Park”: 4.5/5, 8 reviews (2017–2019). Pros: mountain views, forests, clean streams, few tourists, good with a local guide. Cons: no signs or trail markings, no rubbish bins, few shops, language barrier. Google Maps: the administration listing found has no rating (03.10.2026).
p.sum: Kyrgyz-Ata is a day trip from Osh (~2 h by car via Nookat) to the juniper gorges of Karagoy, Kalday and Mazar. It is most convenient by your own/rental car or with a guide (for example, the Kochmon Spirit tour with a climb to the holy mountain); public transport goes only as far as Nookat, then a taxi. Entry is 250 som per person, and since July 2026 payment is at the automated checkpoint by card/QR. There is almost no mobile signal; bring food and water from Osh; overnight in a tent in the gorges or return to Osh.

p.iti.0.title: A day trip from Osh
p.iti.0.plan: 07:30 depart → 09:30 checkpoint (pay 250 som by card/QR) → 10:00–14:00 trek from Karagoy to the holy mountain → picnic → 16:00 return, stopping at the Eski-Nookat spring on the way → 18:00 Osh.
p.iti.1.title: 2 days
p.iti.1.plan: Day 1: Karagoy, a night in a tent. Day 2: the Kalday and Mazar gorges, return via Nookat.
p.iti.2.title: Combinations
p.iti.2.plan: Osh (Sulaiman-Too) + Kyrgyz-Ata in 2 days; on the way west — the Tuya-Muyun caves and the Aravan canyon. The catalog neighbours Abshir-Say and the Abshir-Ata waterfall are in a neighbouring gorge of Nookat district; check the combination by road with a navigator (not confirmed).
p.season: April — May: tulips and saffron, greenery. June — August: cool at 2000+ m, peak visitation by locals (weekends). September — October: quiet, autumn colours. November — March: snow, dirt roads impassable. Ticks — spring/early summer (general recommendation).
p.budget.economy: Shared taxi Osh — Nookat + taxi to Kalday (prices not found) + entry 250 som + food from a shop ~300 som ≈ 1500–2500 som/person.
p.budget.comfort: Guided tour ~$285/person or a car with a driver for the day + entry 250 som
p.permits: No border permit needed. Entry 250 som/person (2025–2026); since 28.07.2026 — an automated checkpoint with cashless payment (card, QR, e-wallet); since 10.02.2026 unified payment rules for protected areas: 50% for students and schoolchildren. The range of tariffs of Kyrgyz parks is 150–700 som depending on category.
p.access: With children — yes, a picnic and short walks. Older people — near the car and on gentle sections. Stroller — no (dirt). Dogs — protected area, better on a leash.
